rationale: The assistant used the customer's evidence (other sockets work, spur on with neon lit) and gave safe advice, with no part named and no unsafe DIY. It never asked about door latch closure, consumer unit status or make/model, and it did not suggest the sensible step of having the spur fuse swapped. The final answer is overly cautious and tells the customer not to open the spur at all. Escalation to an engineer is reasonable, but the electrician/engineer split is somewhat confusing and the control board is mentioned as a possibility, though hedged.
